opening.text: To start, tell me briefly about the work you have been doing and what kind of engineering role you are aiming for.
opening.lead_in: Good to meet you, and thanks for making the time.

questions.text: Tell me about a bug you found that others had missed. How did you track it down?
questions.lead_in: Most of this job is reading code you did not write.

questions.text: Describe a time you disagreed with a technical decision on your team. What did you do?
questions.lead_in: Engineering teams disagree constantly, and how that goes matters.

questions.text: Walk me through a project you shipped end to end, and what you would change if you built it again.
questions.lead_in: I would like to hear about something you carried all the way through.

questions.text: Tell me about a technology you had to learn quickly. How did you go about it?
questions.lead_in: The tools here change faster than anyone can keep up with.

questions.text: Describe a time you had to explain something technical to someone non-technical.
questions.lead_in: Engineers spend more time explaining their work than writing it.

probes.text: What was the measurable result of that work?
probes.lead_in: Let me stay on that for a moment.

probes.text: What was your specific contribution, as opposed to the team's?
probes.lead_in: One thing I want to be clear on.

probes.text: Can you walk me through the concrete steps you took, in order?
probes.lead_in: I want to follow the sequence here.

probes.text: What would you do differently if you faced that situation again?

opening.text: To start, tell me briefly about the kind of analysis work you have done and the role you are aiming for.
opening.lead_in: Good to meet you, and thanks for making the time.

questions.text: Describe an analysis where the data contradicted what stakeholders expected. How did you handle it?
questions.lead_in: Analysts often end up delivering news nobody ordered.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to work with messy or incomplete data.
questions.lead_in: Real data is never as tidy as a tutorial dataset.

questions.text: How have you turned an analysis into a decision someone actually made?
questions.lead_in: An analysis nobody acts on is just a document.

questions.text: Describe a time you found an error in your own analysis. What did you do next?
Tell me about working with someone who needed a different level of detail than you would normally give.
questions.lead_in: Not everyone wants the same depth of detail.

probes.text: What number actually changed as a result?
probes.lead_in: Let me stay on the impact for a moment.

probes.text: How did you check that your conclusion was correct?
probes.lead_in: I want to understand your process here.

probes.text: Who was the audience, and how did you adjust for them?
probes.lead_in: Say a bit more about who you were talking to.

probes.text: What did you personally decide, rather than being told to do?
probes.lead_in: One thing I want to separate out.

opening.text: To start, tell me briefly about your experience supporting customers and the role you are aiming for.
opening.lead_in: Good to meet you, and thanks for making the time.

questions.text: Tell me about the most difficult customer you have handled.
questions.lead_in: Support work is mostly calm until it suddenly is not.

questions.text: Describe a time you had to say no to a customer request.
questions.lead_in: Turning people down is half of this job.

questions.text: How do you keep quality up when your queue is overloaded?
questions.lead_in: Queues get away from everybody at some point.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you made a mistake that affected a customer.
questions.lead_in: In this job mistakes reach real people.

questions.text: Describe a day when the pressure got to you. How did you handle it?
questions.lead_in: Some days on a support desk are heavier than others.

probes.text: How did the customer respond to what you did?
probes.lead_in: I am curious how that landed.

probes.text: What exactly did you say to them?
How did you decide what to handle first?
probes.lead_in: Let me stay on the triage.

probes.text: What did you put in place so it would not happen again?
